DGR sponsorship letter. 2. Integrity Pact on a non judicial stamp paper of Rs. 100/- 3. Empanelment Certificate issued by DGR 4. PAN card of the ESM Corp/Pvt Ltd/Individual Company (as per the details given in DGR Sponsorship Lette r) 5. Self attested copy of valid PF Registration Certificate, if already registered. 6. Self attested copy of valid ESI Registration Certificate if the area is covered under ESI Act and the agenc y is already registered. 7. License of operation in the state of operation of the Security Agency [as per Office Memorandum no. 28( 75)/2020-D(Res-1) dtd. 13.05.2021 and its Corrigendum dtd. 23.06.2021 of Department of Ex-Serviceman Welfare, Ministry of Defence] 8. POWER OF ATTORNEY (POA)/KMP (AS PER THE FORMAT PROVIDED IN THE DOCUMENT) 1 Every establishment has its own locational constraints, topographic requirements, and law & order scen arios. Security deployment should be planned according to local needs and norms. The concerned POWER GRID official must be part of the security deployment plan. 2 Security personnel should patrol designated pathways at least 2–3 times during both day and night. 3 The maximum tenure of a security guard at any POWERGRID location should be limited to 4 years to avo id complacency. 4 When a new security agency takes over, security guards from the previous agency should not continue with the new agency, as long association may lead to complacency and possible leakage of sensitive infor mation. 5 Security guards deployed should preferably be not more than 55 years of age and should have an ex-ar my or paramilitary background. 6 Regular training and fitness programs for security guards should be conducted quarterly, including joggi ng, push-ups, weapon handling, etc., followed by fitness tests. 7 Quarterly mock drills should be conducted under simulated conditions such as fire incidents or catching burglars/thieves red-handed. SOPs should be documented and available at strategic locations. 8 Adequate availability of batons, torches, whistles, umbrellas, and raincoats must be ensured through the contracting agency.

9 The deployment location of each security guard should be clearly defined within the substation premises . 10 All security guards must have the contact details of the nearest police station and fire brigade, includin g the name of the contact person, saved in their mobile phones. 11 Surprise checks should be conducted periodically to verify the readiness and availability of security gua rds at their assigned positions. 12 Quarterly meetings with the owner of the security agency should be conducted, with a feedback mecha nism in place. Minutes of the meeting should be recorded. 13 If an employee is going out of station, a protocol should be established for informing Security and the St ation In-Charge. Increased patrolling of the employee’s residence should be carried out during the period o f absence. . 2. Buyer Added Bid Specific ATC Buyer uploaded ATC document Click here to view the file.
